title: The Golden Joystick Awards Ultimate Game of the Year voting is a-go, with games like Crimson Desert, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Big Walk all on the docket
body: The Golden Joystick Awards' Ultimate Game of the Year voting is now open —celebrating its 44th consecutive year, the votes will remain open until 8 pm ET / 12 am GMT, October 30. It's a stacked roster of nominations this year—with some of our own favourites here at PC Gamer listed to take the crown. Here's an official list of the nominations: 007 First Light Big Walk CONTROL Resonant Crimson Desert Dispatch Forza Horizon 6 Phantom Blade: Zero Pokémon Pokopia PRAGMATA Resident Evil Requiem STAR WARS: Galactic Racer The Blood of Dawnwalker Speaking personally, it's a tough one for me to pick— Crimson Desert is maybe the most technically impressive in terms of scope, releasing with not only a billion systems but also receiving massive updates over the course of the year. So many, in fact, I'm sort of wondering when anyone else at Pearl Abyss is gonna take a break. Star Wars: Galactic Racer has devoured hours of my time, and I've been playing it so much I've developed a new callus on my thumb, whereas Dispatch was a short-but-sweet romp and one of my favourite superhero stories in recent memory. title: Are we in the cozy gaming gold rush era? 'Cozy' has grown over 250% on Steam and 200% in my inbox since 2024
summary: Uh oh, everything is cozy now.
body: Cozy games on Google The past five years of search demand on Google for cozy games, relaxing games, and casual games. Google Trends Interestingly, the resurgence of "casual games" is even more pronounced at a worldwide view. Google Trends First let's check back in on the same Google Search data I pulled in 2023 to compare how much we, the audience, are actually seeking cozy games. We're looking at the past five years or search interest for the terms: cozy games, relaxing games, and casual games. The main term "cozy games" is twice as popular as it was in 2023 when I identified the surprising spike the phrase had already experienced between 2020 and 2023. Google doesn't share raw search volume so this is all relative, not absolute, but it's still clear evidence that the interest in cozy games has continued to explode. What is surprising to me is the comeback for the phrase "casual games." It's one we used a lot in the late twenty-teens but was eclipsed by "cozy" around 2022. Anecdotally, I think "casual" suffered from also being pejorative and may have fallen away in favor of the more positive tone "cozy."
